# MNKAI-III — Deep Analysis: Competitive Positioning & Improvement Roadmap
*Generated by a 7-agent literature/benchmark study (with web sources) on training completion.*

## TL;DR (the honest verdict)
**MNKAI-III is *not* a state-of-the-art-accuracy system — and shouldn't be sold as one.** On raw accuracy it's mid-pack on the 9-class base and behind on the 25-class Indian long-tail. **Where it genuinely leads the field is rigour and transparency:** patient-disjoint (zero-leakage) validation, single-shot external testing, full calibration + conformal reporting that almost no competitor publishes, a real per-Fitzpatrick fairness metric, and a documented majority-class-collapse fix.

> **One-line positioning:** *"Not the highest-accuracy dermatology model, but among the most rigorously and transparently evaluated — the first to pair an Indian long-tail correction with leakage-free external testing, calibration, and uncertainty quantification."*

## Where we stand vs published work

| Dimension | MNKAI-III | Published comparators | Read |
|---|---|---|---|
| **9-class base** | macro-F1 **0.637 ± 0.009**, AUROC ~0.95 (patient-disjoint) | HAM10000/ISIC leaderboards ~0.85–0.93 F1 (but **image-level splits → leakage**); ISIC-2019 winner 0.636 *balanced-acc* | Mid-pack on raw F1; our lower number partly *because* we enforce honest splits |
| **25-class Indian** | macro-F1 **0.484**, top-3 **0.725** (external) | DermaCon-IN 8-class 70.4% acc; Google DLS 26-cond top-3 **93%**; SD-198 198-class ~50–58%; long-tail triage top-3 ~75% | Behind on accuracy, but harder label space; our top-3 ≈ triage benchmark |
| **Melanoma** | recall **0.842**, AUROC **0.987** | FDA-cleared AUROC band 0.958–0.988; dermatologist AUROC 0.78–0.91; commercial sens target ~0.95 | AUROC **top-tier**; recall leaves ~16% miss → screening aid, not autonomous |
| **Fairness** | FST I–III 0.245 vs IV–VI 0.209 (n=777) | Meta-analysis FST I–III AUROC 0.89 vs IV–VI 0.82; DDI shows up to 3× gaps | We *report* it (most don't), but **underpowered** — can't conclude |
| **Calibration/uncertainty** | ECE 0.176→**0.016**, conformal cov 0.984 | Virtually **none** of the comparators report this | **Clear differentiator — we're ahead** |

### Ahead of the field
- ✅ Patient-disjoint group-aware CV (zero leakage) — most SOTA uses leaky image-level splits.
- ✅ Single-shot **external test** (5,886 imgs) — the harder, honest protocol.
- ✅ Full **calibration + conformal** reporting — almost universally omitted.
- ✅ A reported **per-Fitzpatrick fairness** metric.
- ✅ Documented **collapse-and-fix** (eczema 0.004 → 0.503) — a reproducible methods contribution.
- ✅ No synthetic/scraped data; multimodal; on a single 6 GB laptop.

### Behind / must improve
- ❌ Long-tail classes not yet usable: psoriasis 0.16, contact-dermatitis 0.15, bacterial 0.09.
- ❌ Melanoma recall 0.842 (~16% miss) — below the 0.95 screening target.
- ❌ Fairness underpowered (n=777, melanoma not skin-tone-stratified).
- ❌ No biopsy confirmation; prospective pilot not yet done.

### ⚠️ Must-fix framing before submitting
1. **Do not claim "beats the ISIC-2019 winner"** — that compares our macro-F1 to their *balanced accuracy* (apples-to-oranges). Drop or reframe.
2. **Don't imply the long-tail/fairness results are deployment-ready.**
3. **Explicitly state the ~16% melanoma miss rate** and the underpowered (n=777) fairness subsample.

## Improvement roadmap (prioritised by yield ÷ effort)

| # | Improvement | Expected gain | Effort | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Decoupled cRT** — freeze backbone, re-init + retrain only the head with class-balanced sampling (Kang 2020). Infra already exists (`freeze_backbone_epochs` + head-reinit). | macro-F1 **0.484 → 0.50–0.53**; weak-class recall roughly doubles | **Low** (~1 day, head-only, fits 6 GB) | Low (non-destructive) |
| **2** | **Per-class thresholds** instead of argmax (tune on OOF val, freeze for test). `_screening_thresholds.py` already exists. | **+2–4 pts** macro-F1 from rare-class F1 | **Very low** (~½ day) | Low (must not tune on test) |
| **3** | **Lock melanoma operating point** at sensitivity ≥ 0.90 (AUROC 0.987 makes this near-certain). | mel recall **0.842 → 0.90–0.93** | **Very low** (~½ day) | Low (spec/PPV trade-off, report it) |
| **4** | **License-clean data expansion** → DermaCon-IN full (downloader exists), DDI (dark-skin, biopsy-confirmed), SCIN-full. Through the group-aware splitter only. | Biggest ceiling: macro-F1 → **0.52–0.56**; the *only* way to de-underpower fairness | **Med–high** (days each + retrain) | Med (taxonomy mismatch, domain shift, de-dup) |
| **5** | **Hierarchical coarse→fine loss** (super-class head + consistency penalty). | **+1–3 pts**, suppresses cross-super-class confusion; bonus coarse triage metric | **Med** (~2–3 days, new code) | Med (taxonomy + λ tuning) |
| **6** | **Single-mechanism ablation + DRW** (sweep balanced-softmax τ / LDAM margin + deferred reweighting). Ablation driver already built. | **+1–3 pts** (overlaps #1) | **Low–med** (mostly GPU) | Low (config-only) |
| **7** | **Fairness hardening** — group temperature scaling for FST IV–VI + FST-tier oversampling (both wired); gated on #4 data. | dark-skin calibration + balanced-acc up once n grows | **Med** (gated on data) | Med (tiny-slice noise) |

**Recommended sequence:** #2 + #3 first (a day, near-free gains + the melanoma-safety headline) → #1 cRT (the single biggest method lever) → #6 to confirm the best base mechanism → then #4 data expansion (the real ceiling-raiser + the fairness fix) → #5/#7 for the paper's novelty + fairness story.

**Most likely realistic ceiling with #1–3 + #6 (no new data): macro-F1 ~0.52–0.55, melanoma sensitivity ~0.92.** With data expansion (#4): ~0.55–0.58 and a *defensible* fairness result.
